messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 | serving-runtime | latency-spike detected in us-west-2 (p90 requests > 1.2s) — routing to #eng-oncall. Trace: https://telemetry.redwood/trace/abc123 :rotating_light:
Sam K.: seeing the alert, jumping in. Can folks check if this is autoscaler activity or a kernel/oom on the GPU nodes?
Priya R.: I can pull the last 10m of scheduler events, grabbing now.
Jordan L.: I already see a burst of requests to model 'rw-7b-quant' around 00:12 UTC — lots of concurrent short chat completions. Could be a caching miss.
Anika S.: Oncall, confirming customer-facing errors? Any 5xx uptick?
Sam K.: No bulk 5xx in the first 2m, mostly latency. A few timed-out websocket clients but not full error storm.
Luis M.: oncall note: paging docs say p95 > 800ms for 2min triggers — this fits. I'm going to scale additional dedicated pools manually while we triage.
Sam K.: Thanks Luis. Priya, paste scheduler logs when you have them.
Priya R.: scheduler snippet:
```
2026-02-12T00:11:58Z scheduler: scale-up initiated pool=dedicated-rw-01 reason=queue-depth
2026-02-12T00:12:05Z runtime: routing fallback to quant-variant model=rw-7b-quant-v2
2026-02-12T00:12:07Z node: high-kvcache-miss count=487
```
Jordan L.: kvcache-miss spiking explains token re-compute. Looks like prefix caching wasn't applied for a subset of requests (maybe new prompt formats).
Anika S.: I can patch a temporary route policy to favor cached instances and add a safety limit on batching to keep latency down. Want me to push?
Sam K.: Yes, push the policy, but keep the canary flag on. Use `route:prefer=cached` and monitor.
Anika S.: Doing now. Command I ran:
```
redwoodctl route update --model rw-7b-quant --policy prefer-cached --canary=true
```
incident-bot: action | route update succeeded (canary=1/3 nodes).
Priya R.: after route change p90 dropped to ~450ms within 45s. KV miss count falling.
Luis M.: good. I'm leaving additional capacity to spin down gradually.
Sam K.: Customer impact: partial latency degradation for users in us-west-2 for ~3 minutes, no widespread errors. Flagging as SEV2 and we should run a short postmortem.
Jordan L.: I'll open the postmortem doc and assign initial timeline.
Sam K.: please include a brief customer impact blurb: "Transient latency spike affecting chat apps in us-west-2; peak p90 ~1.2s, impact window ~00:11-00:14 UTC. No data loss, no sustained 5xx".
Jordan L.: Created postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/pm/1792003456-pager-bridge-ops-sweep — added sections: timeline, impact, root-cause hypothesis, mitigations, action items.
Anika S.: Action item proposal: 1) make prefix-cache opt-in detection for new prompt formats (owner: Priya) 2) tighten autoscaler cooldown to avoid undershoot (owner: Luis) 3) add route-canary fallback health metric to console (owner: Sam).
Priya R.: I can take item 1. Adding details: detect prompt schema mismatches at ingress and set cache-key hash to normalized form. Estimate 3d.
Luis M.: I'll take item 2; could be 2-3 days to validate in staging and then apply.
Sam K.: I'll own item 3 and add the dashboard card + alert thresholds.
eng-oncall: Quick on-call handoff note: I'll include this incident in today's 08:00 handoff and mention the action owners.
Priya R.: Also recommending a small runbook update: add a troubleshooting checklist for KV-cache miss signatures (logs to grep, telemetry markers). Should we create a runbook PR?
Jordan L.: Yes, go ahead. Link: https://infra.redwood/runbooks/kvcache-troubleshoot. I'll add a placeholder and tag @Priya R. for content.
Anika S.: For follow-ups, request: add a test in the integration harness simulating mixed prompt formats to ensure cache-key normalization keeps hit rates high. (owner: Anika)
Sam K.: Good. Also let's add a short blameless note in the customer-status channel: no outage, transient latency, being tracked. I'll draft.
Luis M.: Drafted message: "Heads up — short latency spike in us-west-2, now mitigated. Working on follow-ups. If you see customer complaints, escalate to support #support-escalations."
Sam K.: Postmortem meeting: propose 48h from now for a 30-minute sync to go over action items and timeline review. Who's available?
Priya R.: I can do 48h.
Jordan L.: available.
Anika S.: available.
Luis M.: yes.
Sam K.: Scheduling meeting and will attach pre-read (postmortem draft).
incident-bot: followup | postmortem scheduled: 2026-02-14T00:20:00Z — calendar invite sent to participants.
Sam K.: After the meeting we'll update the runbook and close action items in the tracker. Thanks all for quick response :thumbsup:
Priya R.: small note for runbook PR: include a short snippet for `redwoodctl` to force a route canary rollback:
```
redwoodctl route update --model rw-7b-quant --policy prefer-cached --canary=false
```
Jordan L.: I'll track the action items in the incident tracker and mark owners + due dates.
Anika S.: adding a test card to the CI board now.
Luis M.: once actions are in tracker, I'll close the incident channel thread.
Sam K.: Closing comment: good triage and quick mitigation. We'll iterate on the playbook items flagged.
eng-oncall: please close this thread after the postmortem meeting and after runbook PR lands."
